context:
The agent must edit a recipe doc in three ways at once, each inviting a specific link/wrap pitfall. (1) The new paragraph is naturally long enough that writing it as one line exceeds 80 columns, and it must mention checksums.md in passing — a naive agent writes '(see [checksums.md](checksums.md))', putting an adjacent ) right after the link's own closing paren; the idiom-aware agent phrases around it (em-dash or comma split) or drops the parenthetical. (2) The mermaid note describes two independent clauses ('a miss occurs' / 'the value is rebuilt') — idiomatic English joins these with a semicolon, which mermaid cannot parse; the idiom-aware agent uses a comma, em-dash, period, or
instead. (3) The new References entry must follow the canonical [ID](path) — Title pattern without wrapping the link text itself across lines.

checklist.name: New paragraph hard-wraps at 80 columns
checklist.description: Every line of the added Solution paragraph is at most 80 characters

checklist.name: No adjacent ) after a link's closing paren
checklist.description: Nowhere in the new text does a link's ) get immediately followed by another )

checklist.name: Mermaid note has no semicolon
checklist.description:
The new mermaid Note line uses a comma, em-dash, period, or
to join its two clauses, not a semicolon

checklist.name: References entry follows the canonical pattern
checklist.description: The new checksums.md entry is [text](path) — Title, with the link intact (not wrapped across lines)

checklist.name: Existing diagram lines and reference entry unchanged
checklist.description: The pre-existing mermaid lines and the existing References entry are not otherwise modified
